<reason>CON built a genuinely creative case (the fee doesn't exist yet; itemization at checkout preserves context; early sticker shock harms the service-charge wage model), and its "precision is what makes decision possible" frame gave it a real route. But PRO neutralized the load-bearing mechanism early with the rate-card answer: state fixed charges as numbers, variable ones as their governing rule, and the computed figure the moment inputs exist. That reply held for the rest of the debate, and it exposed CON's repeated attack on "bullhorn" browsing-screen banners as aimed at a rule PRO never proposed. PRO's Q1 also forced a damaging concession: CON admitted flat 18% charges and per-ticket schedules are already routinely posted, which simultaneously grants the practice the motion demands and gutted CON's burden/compliance-cost objection, leaving CON defending secrecy only for the "harder" residue. CON's fallback — that formulas are "homework" and incomparable across tabs — is its best late move, but PRO's answer that a diner choosing where to eat needs to know an 18% mandatory charge applies, not the final cent, was the better weighing. On the leverage clash, CON's "you can still close the tab" was answered persuasively by the sunk-cost/countdown framing and the "receipt, not information" line; CON never really dislodged it. PRO also carried the cleaner burden-allocation weighing (the party who authored the formula should state it). PRO's clipped Rebuttal 1 is a real execution cost, and CON deserves credit for answering Q2 honestly rather than dodging, but PRO made the decisive clash easier to resolve.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Q1 and the follow-up on it: forcing CON to concede that flat service charges and per-ticket fee schedules are fixed and already posted, then showing that this concedes the motion's core practice while leaving CON defending concealment only for the hardest residual cases — combined with the rate-card reply that dissolved CON's "the number doesn't exist yet" mechanism without requiring any false estimate.</best_rebuttal>
